summary: Bangladesh’s forestry pledges combine restoration and conservation. It aims for 24% tree cover, restoration of 230,000 ha of deforested sal forest, and 100,000 ha of afforestation/reforestation across coastal, island and degraded lands, while maintaining forest cover through 72,000 ha of protected-area co-management and 79,000 ha of sustainable forest-management and livelihood activities. Other restoration includes 10 million tree saplings and 2,725.1 ha of rehabilitated marshland. Agriculture pledges include separate AWD area targets of 50,000 ha and 100,000 ha, rice-varietal improvement across 2,129,000 ha, 30% coverage under both AWD and short-duration rice varieties, 1.882 million large ruminants, 107,000 mini-biogas plants, 30% improved manure management, and crossbred dairy-cow feed-improvement targets of 0.2 million and 1.5 million. The rice-varietal target equals about 20.3% of 2022 agricultural land, while sal-forest restoration equals about 16.7% of 2022 forest cover.
